# fshy: CI runners in full

> Hosted CI runners and registries, and what they will run.

Data as of 2026-11-10, the date of the published data. Version `e7cf1b4a40af`: the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of every record's Markdown, topic by topic in the one order (hosted before self-hosted, then verdict, provider name, record id); it changes whenever a record does.

How to read a record, and the other topics: https://fshy.ajam.dev/llms-full.txt. One line per record: https://fshy.ajam.dev/t/ci-cd-runners.md.

## Appcircle

- `ci-cd-runners/appcircle-starter` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding request-rate | category CI runner | tier Starter
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-09T12:52:26.539Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-10
- url https://appcircle.io/pricing | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/appcircle.md
- free tier: Starter, labelled Always Free: 20 builds per month, 1 concurrent build, 30 minutes max build time per build | unit: mixed | metered on: unstated | read on: 2026-11-02 | source: [1] | note: the pool is a count of builds a month, not minutes or credits; no term of the unit vocabulary names a build count
- per-object cap: 30 minutes max build time per build | source: [1]
- retention: not stated | source: [1]
- egress: not stated | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: registration is by email address and password at my.appcircle.io, signing up with the Sign up with Company E-mail button and then verifying the address; common and disposable email domains cannot be used, so a company address is required. No card and no phone number is named on the registration page
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): 20 builds per month on Starter [1]
  - request-rate (binding): 1 concurrent build [1]
  - per-object-cap: 30 minutes max build time per build [1]
- binding note: the 20-builds-a-month pool fails first (at most 600 build minutes a month, which is a compute pool counted in builds); the schema has no term for a build-count or compute-time pool, so request-rate is the nearest
- interface detail: a hosted mobile CI/CD service with build, signing, distribution and store-publishing modules, and a REST API at api.appcircle.io authenticated by a Personal Access Key or an API Key, with the API reference published as an OpenAPI document
- tooling: builds for iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter on Apple Silicon machines, with a clean isolated environment for every build
- composes with: not stated
- reliability: no reliability event recorded
- notes: a mobile-only CI service: builds run on Apple Silicon machines, so the Starter pool is also a route to macOS build time. 20 builds of at most 30 minutes is a ceiling of 600 build minutes a month.
- evidence note: the pricing page was read on 2026-11-02 and states the Starter pool, concurrency and build time; what registration asks for is unverified
- extras:
  - derived: 20 builds x 30 minutes = 600 build minutes a month at most

## AppVeyor

- `ci-cd-runners/appveyor` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding per-object-cap | category CI runner
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-04T06:00:42.533Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-05
- url https://www.appveyor.com/pricing/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/appveyor.md
- free tier: an Open-source plan at USD 0 listing 'Unlimited public projects', 1 concurrent job and 5 self-hosted jobs, with a 60-minute maximum build; the page states no monthly minute allowance for that plan, and does not use the word unlimited for builds or minutes | unit: objects | metered on: wall-clock | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: 60 minutes per build on the free plan; one concurrent job | source: [1]
- retention: build artifacts and history are retained per project settings | source: [1]
- egress: no egress charge published | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: email or GitHub OAuth
- interface: git, cli
- limits:
  - per-object-cap (binding): 60 minutes per build; one concurrent job on Free [1]
- interface detail: an appveyor.yml or the web UI; a REST API
- tooling: Windows and Linux images; MSBuild, Visual Studio, and the usual package managers
- composes with: the cheapest way to get a real Windows build, which no other free tier here offers at this cap
- reliability: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
- notes: Sixty minutes and one job at a time is a build system for a small project. It is not general compute, and the concurrency of one is the number that ends that idea.
- evidence note: the pricing page was read on 2026-10-22. The page's unlimited claim is about the number of public projects, not about the number of builds, which the page does not state.
- evidence:
  - [1] 2026-10-22: public open-source projects build without a minute cap, with one concurrent job and a 60-minute maximum build

  - [1] 2026-11-04: every plan caps a build job at 60 minutes | capture: sha256:2697e53f1fcee2f3591a1e60fbb56d82d22cf449376de2ada38313790b34ffe8 | quote: All plans have maximum build job execution time of 60 minutes.

## Azure Pipelines (private project, free grant)

- `ci-cd-runners/azure-pipelines-private` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding per-object-cap | category CI runner
- needs card yes, phone yes, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-03T00:32:24.304Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-04
- url https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/agents/hosted | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/microsoft.md
- disagrees on verdict: `ci-cd-runners/azure-pipelines-private` says qualifies-with-caveat, `ci-cd-runners/azure-pipelines-public` says dead
- free tier: 1 free parallel job with 1,800 minutes a month and 60 minutes per job, with a 10 GB disk | unit: minutes | metered on: wall-clock | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: 60 minutes per job on the free grant; 360 minutes only on a paid parallel job | source: [1]
- retention: artifacts and logs follow pipeline retention settings; the minute pool is monthly | source: [1]
- egress: no egress charge on the hosted agent itself | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: card | detail: the free grant applies only to an Azure DevOps organisation linked to a valid Azure subscription; Azure DevOps billing does not accept the Azure Free Trial, and an Azure account asks for a phone number and a non-prepaid credit or debit card
- interface: git, cli
- limits:
  - per-object-cap (binding): 60 minutes per job on the free grant [1]
  - request-rate: 1,800 minutes a month with 1 free parallel job [1]
- interface detail: an azure-pipelines.yml pipeline; a REST API and the az CLI
- tooling: the Microsoft-hosted images; any shell; the Azure CLI preinstalled
- composes with: 1,800 minutes is the largest per-job-minute pool of the small providers, and the 60-minute job cap is the smallest
- reliability: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
- notes: Each job on the free grant stops at 60 minutes and the grant ends at 1,800 minutes a month; a paid parallel job lifts the job cap to 360 minutes. The same organisation grant includes one self-hosted parallel job with no time limit, which runs the agent on a machine the user provides.
- evidence note: the hosted-agents doc was read.

## Buildkite Free

- `ci-cd-runners/buildkite-free` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding volume-quota | category CI runner
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-03T00:32:22.884Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-04
- url https://buildkite.com/pricing | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/buildkite.md
- price USD 0.004 per vCPU-minute
- free tier: 5 users, 10 concurrent jobs and 2,000 Linux vCPU-minutes a month, plus 250,000 test executions a month | unit: minutes | metered on: wall-clock | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: 10 GiB per artifact uploaded from an agent, and 50 GiB of artifacts in one job's upload batch | bytes: 10737418240
- retention: builds are stored 30 days on the Free plan (90 on Pro, 365 on Enterprise) and artifacts 30 days; the vCPU-minute pool is monthly | days: 30 | source: [1]
- egress: artifact downloads: 250 GB a month on the Free plan, 2.5 TB a month on Pro and then USD 0.10 per GB; no charge for network traffic from a hosted agent is published on the pricing, limits or hosted-agent pages | metered: yes | free allowance: 250 GB a month of artifact downloads | price per TB: USD 100 per TB of artifact downloads beyond the Pro allowance; the Free plan names no overage | source: [2]
- identity: email | detail: the signup form asks for a full name, an email and a password, or a GitHub sign-in; the Free plan states 'No credit card required'; the form has no phone or card field
- interface: git, cli
- limits:
  - volume-quota (binding): Up to 2,000 Linux vCPU-minutes a month of Buildkite-hosted agents on the Free plan (Pro includes 4,000); usage is the shape's vCPU count times job runtime [3]
  - request-rate: 5 users on Free [1]
  - request-rate: Linux hosted-agent concurrency of 20 vCPU on the Free plan, which is 10 small machines at 2 vCPU each; further jobs queue until capacity frees [3]
  - retention-clamped: Job timeout of 4 hours on the Free plan; unlimited on Pro and Enterprise [3]
- binding note: the monthly pool runs out first: 2,000 vCPU-minutes on the only shape the Free plan offers, 2 vCPU, is 1,000 wall-clock minutes a month, against a 4-hour job timeout; usage counts job runtime, with startup and shutdown excluded
- interface detail: an agent you run, with Buildkite as the control plane; the bk CLI and a REST API
- tooling: Buildkite-hosted Linux agents on the Free plan, small shape only, run the jobs with no machine of the user's; their outbound traffic comes from IP address ranges shared across customers, and dedicated static addresses are requested from Support; the buildkite-agent binary can also run on a VM from another provider and take jobs from the same pipelines
- composes with: the Free plan supplies both the scheduler and a hosted machine; once the monthly vCPU-minute pool is spent, the same pipelines can dispatch to a buildkite-agent on a free or rented VM from another provider, which counts against the 10 concurrent self-hosted jobs rather than the pool
- reliability: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
- notes: 2,000 vCPU-minutes is 33 vCPU-hours. The Free plan reaches only the 2 vCPU small shape, so the pool is 1,000 wall-clock minutes (16 h 40 min) a month, and a larger shape needs a paid plan. A self-run agent does not draw on the pool, but it needs a machine from another provider, so it is the last resort.
- evidence note: the pricing page was read and lists the Free column explicitly.
- evidence:
  - [1] 2026-10-22: the Free column: 'Up to 2,000 Linux vCPU minutes per month', 'Up to 250k test executions per month', 10 concurrent agents with 10 included, 5 users; Pro includes 4,000 Linux vCPU minutes
  - [1] 2026-10-22: Free: up to 5 users, up to 10 concurrent jobs, up to 2,000 Linux vCPU-minutes a month; hosted agents at USD 0.004 per vCPU-minute, metered to the second with no minimum

## CircleCI Free

- `ci-cd-runners/circleci-free` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding request-rate | category CI runner
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-10-30T12:41:30.391Z (live) | stale on 2026-11-30
- url https://circleci.com/pricing/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/circleci.md
- free tier: 30,000 credits a month on the Free plan, with up to 5 active users and 30x concurrency; open-source projects get up to 400,000 credits a month for Linux, Arm and Docker builds, and macOS and Windows open-source builds draw on the 30,000 | unit: credits | metered on: wall-clock | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: 1 hour maximum job runtime on the Free plan; 3 hours on Performance and 5 hours on Scale
- retention: credits expire monthly and do not roll over; caches and artifacts expire per configuration | source: [2]
- egress: network transfer is billed only for traffic from CircleCI to self-hosted runners; the Free plan includes 1 GB of network transfer and 2 GB-months of storage, and use beyond these draws from the monthly credits at 420 credits per GB | metered: no | source: [2]
- identity: email | detail: an email address and a password, verified by email, for GitHub, GitLab or Cursor Origin projects; a Bitbucket account for Bitbucket Cloud projects; the Free plan needs no credit card
- interface: git, cli
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): 30,000 credits a month on Free; every credit expires at the end of the month [1]
  - request-rate (binding): 30x concurrency on Free, and 5 active users [1]
  - per-object-cap: 1 hour maximum job runtime on the Free plan [3]
- interface detail: a .circleci/config.yml pipeline; the CircleCI API and CLI
- tooling: the CircleCI convenience images; docker; any shell
- composes with: the largest credit pool of the hosted CI providers here, and the only one that scales with public rather than private visibility by a factor above ten
- reliability: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
- notes: Every job on the Free plan stops at 1 hour, so both the 400,000-credit open-source pool and the 30,000-credit pool are spent in jobs of at most 1 hour. The vendor's credits page gives the macOS open-source allowance as 30,000 credits a month in one section and 25,000 in another, so that figure is unsettled.
- evidence note: the pricing page was read; the credits doc was read for the overage rate. The 5,000-credit figure in circulation is the pre-2025 plan.
- evidence:
  - [1] 2026-10-22: Free: 30,000 credits a month, 5 active users, 30x concurrency; 400,000 credits a month for public repositories
  - [2] 2026-10-22: credits are consumed by machine size and duration; network and storage beyond the threshold are 420 credits per GB

## Cloudflare Pages builds

- `ci-cd-runners/cloudflare-pages-builds` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding volume-quota | category CI runner | tier Pages Free
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-04T06:00:42.534Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-05
- url https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/platform/limits/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/cloudflare.md
- free tier: Free plan: 500 builds a month, 1 build at a time, 20 minutes per build. Pro: 5,000 builds a month and 5 concurrent builds. Business: 20,000 builds a month and 20 concurrent builds | unit: mixed | metered on: unstated | read on: 2026-11-02 | source: [1] | note: the quota counts builds, not minutes: a one-minute build and a twenty-minute build each use one of the 500; the vocabulary has no builds term for the unit, so mixed stands in
- per-object cap: 20 minutes per build | source: [1]
- retention: unverified: the limits and build pages state no retention period for builds or build logs | source: [1]
- egress: not stated for the build container; the output of a build is a Pages deployment | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: a Cloudflare account opened with an email address and a password, verified by email; a GitHub or GitLab account authorised to Cloudflare for Git builds
- interface: git, rest
- limits:
  - volume-quota (binding): 500 builds a month on Free; 5,000 on Pro; 20,000 on Business [1]
  - request-rate: 1 build at a time per account on Free; 5 on Pro; 20 on Business [1]
  - per-object-cap: 20 minutes per build [1]
- limits note: only GitHub and GitLab repositories connect; a project connected to Git cannot switch to Direct Upload later
- binding note: the 500 monthly builds are spent by pushes and Deploy Hook calls whatever their length, so a busy repository reaches the count before the 20-minute cap matters
- interface detail: a push to a connected GitHub or GitLab repository builds and deploys the project; a Deploy Hook is a unique URL that starts a build for one branch on an HTTP POST
- endpoint: unverified: the Deploy Hook URL is generated per hook in the dashboard and its format is not stated on the page read
- tooling: a gVisor container with Ruby, Node.js, Python, PHP and Go preinstalled and versions overridable by environment variable or version file; the user supplies a build command and an output directory
- composes with: a 20-minute job on every push or Deploy Hook call, ending in a Pages deployment. An external scheduler calling a Deploy Hook makes it a scheduled job, but each call spends one of the 500 monthly builds. Builds run by an external CI system and uploaded with Wrangler direct upload do not use the Pages build runner; Cloudflare Workers Builds is a separate service with its own record
- reliability: unverified: no page read states what happens to a Free account once the 500 monthly builds are used
- notes: A Git-driven build service whose job is bound to a Pages deployment: the build command writes an output directory that is deployed. Pro plan price is unverified; no page read states it. A separate Cloudflare service, Workers Builds, offers 3,000 build minutes a month on Free and has its own record.
- evidence note: every number is quoted from the Cloudflare Pages limits page; no build was run, so CPU, memory and disk of the build container, outbound network access from it and what happens to a build after the 500 monthly builds are spent are unverified

## Cloudflare Workers Builds

- `ci-cd-runners/cloudflare-workers-builds` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding per-object-cap | category CI runner | tier free
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-04T06:00:40.517Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-05
- url https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/builds/limits-and-pricing/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/cloudflare.md
- free tier: Workers Free: 3,000 build minutes a month, 1 concurrent build, 20 minutes per build, 2 vCPU, 8 GB memory and 20 GB disk. Workers Paid (USD 5 a month minimum): 6,000 build minutes a month, then USD 0.005 per minute, 6 concurrent builds, 4 vCPU | unit: minutes | metered on: wall-clock | read on: 2026-10-30 | source: [1] | note: a build minute is the time a project takes to build; the overage price applies on Paid plans only; the Builds API reports whether the build-minute allowance is exhausted and when it refreshes, for non-paid plans only; what a push does once the Free minutes are spent (queued, refused or billed) is unverified: behind a sign-up
- per-object cap: 20 minutes per build on every plan; 8 GB memory and 20 GB disk per build; 64 environment variables per Worker | source: [1]
- retention: builds and build logs are kept 90 days after the build finishes; the versions and deployments a build created are not removed | days: 90 | source: [1]
- egress: build commands make HTTPS requests and the build image checks their certificates; no page states whether the build container's outbound traffic is restricted or unrestricted (unverified: no build was run); the build's output is a Worker, and the Workers Paid plan states no additional charge for data transfer (egress) or bandwidth | metered: no | source: [2]
- identity: email | detail: a Cloudflare account opened with an email address and a password, then verified by email; a GitHub, GitLab or Cursor Origin account authorised to Cloudflare, unless the repository is on Cloudflare Artifacts. Workers Paid adds a USD 5 monthly minimum charge
- interface: git, rest
- limits:
  - per-object-cap (binding): 20 minutes per build on Free and Paid; 8 GB memory; 20 GB disk [1]
  - request-rate: 3,000 build minutes a month on Free; 6,000 on Paid, then USD 0.005 per minute [1]
  - request-rate: 1 concurrent build per account on Free, 6 on Paid; Deploy Hooks 10 a minute per Worker and 100 a minute per account [1]
  - retention-clamped: builds and build logs kept 90 days after the build finishes [1]
- limits note: a build fails when the Worker name in the dashboard does not match the name in the Wrangler configuration file; Workers Builds does not honour the custom-build settings of the Wrangler file
- binding note: a job longer than 20 minutes cannot run on any plan, and the 3,000 Free minutes at one concurrent build hold many full-length builds, so the per-build cap fails before the monthly minutes
- interface detail: a push to a connected GitHub, GitLab, Cursor Origin or Cloudflare Artifacts repository runs an optional build command, then a deploy command that defaults to npx wrangler deploy and can be customised; non-production branches run a preview command. A Deploy Hook is a URL that starts a build for one branch on an HTTP POST with no Authorization header
- endpoint: https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/workers/builds/deploy_hooks/<DEPLOY_HOOK_ID>
- tooling: an Ubuntu 24.04 build image with Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby and Go preinstalled and versions overridable by environment variable or version file; the deploy and preview commands are Wrangler commands
- composes with: a 20-minute Ubuntu job on every push or Deploy Hook call, ending in a Worker deploy; an external cron calling a Deploy Hook makes it a scheduled job, and a repository on Cloudflare Artifacts keeps source, build and deploy inside one Cloudflare account. GitHub Actions on a public repository gives longer jobs and comes first
- reliability: only GitHub, GitLab, Cursor Origin and Cloudflare Artifacts repositories connect; GitHub or GitLab instances run by their owners do not
- notes: Confirmed as a CI runner service whose job is bound to a Worker deploy: every production build ends in the deploy command and every other branch in the preview command. Price per minute: USD 0.005 beyond the 6,000 minutes included in the USD 5 Workers Paid plan. Whether the build container has unrestricted outbound network access, and what happens to a build on Free once the 3,000 minutes are spent, are unverified.
- evidence note: every number is quoted from Cloudflare's Workers Builds limits page and the build documentation; no build was run, so network access from the build container and the behaviour once Free minutes are spent are unverified

## GitHub Actions on a private repository

- `ci-cd-runners/github-actions-private` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding request-rate | category CI runner
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-03T17:29:36.354Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-04
- url https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/github.md
- price USD 0.006 per Linux minute beyond the allowance
- free tier: USD 12 of included compute usage per month on GitHub Free and GitHub Free for organizations (the vendor states a monetary amount, not minutes); at USD 0.006 a minute on a standard Linux 2-core runner that is 2,000 minutes per month; USD 18 on Pro and Team, USD 300 on Enterprise Cloud, shared with cloud sandbox compute; 500 MB of artifact storage on Free | unit: credits | metered on: wall-clock | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: 6 hours per job, the same as the public path; the difference is the monthly minute pool | source: [2]
- retention: artifacts kept 90 days by default; the runner is destroyed at the end of the job | days: 90 | source: [3]
- egress: no egress charge; artifact storage is 500 MB on Free and shared with GitHub Packages | metered: yes | free allowance: 500 MB artifact and package storage | source: [4]
- identity: email | detail: a GitHub account; no card while inside the included amounts
- interface: git, cli
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): USD 12 of included compute usage a month on Free, or 2,000 minutes on a standard Linux 2-core runner at USD 0.006 a minute; it resets at the start of each billing cycle, and usage is blocked once it is consumed when no payment method is on file [1]
  - per-object-cap: 6 hours per job; 500 MB of artifact storage shared with Packages on Free [2]
  - request-rate (binding): 20 concurrent jobs on Free [2]
- interface detail: the same workflow YAML; minutes are charged to the repository owner, not the trigger
- tooling: the same runner images as the public path on a smaller machine: on a private repository ubuntu-latest is 2 vCPU, 8 GB RAM and 14 GB SSD, against 4 vCPU and 16 GB RAM on a public repository
- composes with: the honest paid path: 2,000 minutes is 33 hours of one runner a month, and beyond it Linux billing is USD 0.006 a minute
- reliability: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
- notes: 2,000 minutes is 33 hours and the per-job cap still applies, so the two limits are independent and the smaller one wins. A single six-hour job already spends 18% of the month.
- evidence note: the billing page's plan table was read.

## GitHub Actions on a public repository

- `ci-cd-runners/github-actions-public` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding per-object-cap | category CI runner
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-03T17:29:36.355Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-04
- url https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/github.md
- free tier: standard GitHub-hosted runners are free with no minute cap on a public repository; 20 concurrent jobs on Free; 6 hours per job | unit: unlimited | metered on: wall-clock | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: 6 hours of execution per job on a GitHub-hosted runner; 35 days per workflow run including waiting and approval; 256 jobs per matrix per run; a 500 KB workflow file | source: [2] | note: a self-hosted job is capped at 5 days instead
- retention: artifacts and logs are kept 90 days by default and configurable per repository; the runner is destroyed at the end of the job | days: 90 | source: [3]
- egress: no egress charge on the runner; artifact storage is capped at 500 MB on Free and shared with GitHub Packages | metered: yes | free allowance: 500 MB artifact and package storage | source: [4]
- identity: email | detail: a GitHub account; no card for a public repository
- interface: git, cli
- limits:
  - per-object-cap (binding): 6 hours per job; 35 days per workflow run; 256 jobs per matrix; a 500 KB workflow file [2]
  - request-rate: 20 concurrent jobs on GitHub Free (Pro 40, Team 60, Enterprise 500); 5 concurrent macOS [2]
  - retention-clamped: cache entries not accessed in over 7 days are removed [5]
  - retention-clamped: artifacts and logs are kept 90 days by default and the window is configurable per repository [3]
  - per-object-cap (binding): 10 GB of cache per repository, evicted oldest-first beyond it [5]
- limits note: 100 workflow runs may queue per concurrency group; cache uploads are 200 a minute and downloads 1,500 a minute per repository; in a public repository a scheduled workflow is automatically disabled when the repository has no activity for 60 days (docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/disable-and-enable-workflows)
- interface detail: a workflow YAML in .github/workflows, triggered by a push, a schedule, a pull request or a repository dispatch; the runner is a shell with a network
- tooling: the runner image is Ubuntu 24.04 with 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM and 14 GB SSD; any package manager, any compiler, docker buildx
- composes with: free compute whose output has to leave immediately: artifacts are 500 MB, GHCR is 500 MB, and the cache evicts at 7 days. R2's 10 GB free tier is the join that makes the chain storable
- reliability: the repository, its workflows and its logs are public, which is a technical property of the free tier and not a policy question
- notes: Unlimited minutes is true and it is not the number that decides anything. The capacity is the 20-slot concurrency: 20 slots x 24 h is 480 runner-hours a day, which is the flow ceiling, and the 120 runner-hours the slots hold at one instant is a stock and not a rate. Minutes are not scarce; a single job that runs longer than six hours is impossible. A 256-job matrix at the six-hour ceiling is 1,536 runner-hours, or thirteen waves of 20 and 78 hours of wall clock.
- evidence note: the billing and limits pages were read on 2026-10-22 and state both the unlimited public minutes and each cap. No workflow was run, so the concurrency and job-duration figures are the pages' own.
- evidence:

  - [6] 2026-10-22: ubuntu-latest is 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, 14 GB SSD; ubuntu-slim is 1 vCPU and 5 GB

## GitLab Container Registry

- `ci-cd-runners/gitlab-container-registry` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding request-rate | category container registry
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-09T12:09:21.557Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-10
- url https://docs.gitlab.com/user/storage_usage_quotas/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/gitlab.md
- free tier: the registry is excluded from the 10 GiB namespace repository quota; no separate free cap is published | unit: unlimited | metered on: stored-bytes | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: no separate published cap: the container registry is not included in the project storage limit, and the page publishes no cap for it | source: [1]
- retention: tags expire per the project's cleanup policy if one is configured; nothing expires by default | source: [1]
- egress: no egress charge is published; storage is what is metered | metered: yes | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: a GitLab account
- interface: oci, rest
- limits:
  - per-object-cap: storage above the namespace purchased amount is billed; the registry is excluded from the 10 GiB repository quota [1]
- limits note: the 10 GiB figure that circulates is the repository quota and not the registry quota; the two are different limits and the comparison literature conflates them
- interface detail: the OCI distribution API at registry.gitlab.com; docker login with a deploy token or CI job token
- tooling: docker, podman, skopeo
- composes with: the only free registry here that does not count image layers against the same quota as the code
- reliability: the token endpoint answers a pull scope requested without a credential with a 2,596-byte token JSON
- notes: An exclusion is not an allowance. The doc says the registry does not count against 10 GiB; it does not say the registry is free, and no separate free figure is published.
- evidence note: the storage-quota doc was read and states the exclusion.

## RunnerHut

- `ci-cd-runners/runnerhut` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding request-rate | category CI runner (hosted, GitHub Actions-compatible)
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-10T02:39:57.384Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-11
- url https://runnerhut.com/pricing | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/runnerhut.md
- free tier: 3,000 Linux minutes a month on the free plan, with unlimited cache, every runner family and full analytics; per-second billing with a one-minute minimum beyond it. The 2 vCPU Linux x64 runner is USD 0.0040 a minute, the 2 vCPU ARM64 runner USD 0.0032, Windows USD 0.0080, macOS USD 0.0400 and an L4 GPU runner USD 0.0900. | unit: minutes | metered on: wall-clock | read on: 2026-11-10 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: not applicable: a job is bounded by the runner size, and the page prices a 2 vCPU tier and scales linearly with size
- retention: not applicable: a job runs and is destroyed; the page publishes no artifact or cache retention window
- egress: no egress charge is published: the page says it bills per-second compute with no per-developer fee, no cache charges and no egress surprises | metered: no
- identity: email | detail: an email address and a GitHub account to connect a repository: the homepage states "No credit card required · 3,000 free minutes", and no signup was performed
- interface: git
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): 3,000 Linux minutes a month on the free plan [1]
  - request-rate (binding): USD 0.0040 a minute for the 2 vCPU Linux x64 runner, USD 0.0032 for ARM64, USD 0.0900 for an L4 GPU runner [1]
  - request-rate (binding): per-second billing with a one-minute minimum, so a 20-second job is billed as a full minute [1]
- limits note: no concurrency cap, queue charge, cache charge or egress charge is published; the free pool is Linux only and every runner family is available on the paid meter
- binding note: 3,000 minutes is the first thing to fail: on a 2 vCPU runner it is 50 hours of wall-clock time a month, and nothing else on the free plan is capped.
- interface detail: a GitHub Actions workflow points its runs-on label at a RunnerHut runner; the homepage calls them drop-in runners and says there is no agent to install
- tooling: a one-line change to an existing GitHub Actions workflow; no agent, CLI or self-hosted runner is needed
- composes with: GitHub Actions on a public repository stays free and comes first; RunnerHut buys private-repository minutes at USD 0.0040 for 2 vCPU against GitHub list price of USD 0.0060, and the 3,000 free minutes cover a small private pipeline before any card is needed
- reliability: the page publishes no job wall clock, no concurrency cap and no queue limit; per-second billing with a one-minute minimum rounds a short job up to a full minute
- notes: A hosted GitHub Actions runner with a free pool large enough for a small private pipeline: 3,000 Linux minutes a month, no cache charge and no egress charge. The rates undercut GitHub list price on every family the page lists, and the one-minute minimum is the only rounding. The free pool is Linux only, and the runners are EU-hosted with data residency in six regions.
- evidence note: The free pool, the five runner rates and the billing granularity are read from the vendor own pricing page, and the no-card and drop-in claims from its homepage. Raise by running one job on the free plan and reading the minute counter and the first invoice line.

## runners.io

- `ci-cd-runners/runners-io` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding request-rate | category CI runner (hosted, GitHub Actions-compatible)
- needs card yes, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-10T02:39:57.489Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-11
- url https://www.runners.io/pricing | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/runners.md
- free tier: 3,000 run-minutes included every month for every organisation, with no monthly fee; beyond that USD 0.0040 a run-minute. A run-minute is one minute of a 2 vCPU Linux x64 machine, so a 4 vCPU job spends two run-minutes a minute and a 1 vCPU job spends half of one. | unit: minutes | metered on: wall-clock | read on: 2026-11-10 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: not applicable: a job is bounded by the runner size, and the meter is weighted by vCPU count rather than capped per job
- retention: not applicable: a job runs and is destroyed; state that is kept is priced separately at USD 0.50 a GB-month
- egress: no bandwidth charge is published: the pricing page lists queue wait, cold start, control-plane calls and state reads and writes as not billed, and the homepage says the customer pays only for the minutes jobs run | metered: no
- identity: card | detail: a card: the homepage and the pricing page both say "Card required", and the card is charged for the minutes jobs run
- interface: git
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): 3,000 run-minutes a month included, then USD 0.0040 a run-minute [1]
  - per-object-cap: state that is kept is USD 0.50 a GB-month [1]
  - request-rate (binding): a priority label costs twice the run-minutes and twice the rate of the same label [1]
- limits note: the meter is weighted by vCPU: 1 vCPU spends 0.5 run-minutes a minute, 4 vCPU spends 2, 8 vCPU spends 4, Linux ARM64 is 0.625x the same size on x64, and Windows is 2.5x
- binding note: 3,000 run-minutes is the first thing to fail, and the vCPU weighting makes it smaller than it looks: on a 4 vCPU runner it is 1,500 wall-clock minutes a month, and the card requirement gates the account before the pool is spent.
- interface detail: a GitHub Actions workflow changes its runs-on label to a runners.io label such as runnersio-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404; every job runs in its own fresh virtual machine
- tooling: a one-line runs-on change on an existing GitHub Actions workflow; no agent or self-hosted runner is needed
- composes with: GitHub Actions on a public repository stays free and comes first; runners.io buys private-repository minutes at USD 0.0040 for 2 vCPU against GitHub list price of USD 0.0060, and the 3,000 included run-minutes cover a small private pipeline, but a card is required before the first job
- reliability: the page publishes no job wall clock and no concurrency cap; the meter is weighted by vCPU, so a wider runner spends the pool faster, and a priority label doubles both the rate and the run-minutes
- notes: A hosted GitHub Actions runner market that includes 3,000 run-minutes a month for every organisation and meters by vCPU-weighted time rather than by seat. The weighting is the fact a reader must carry: 3,000 run-minutes is 1,500 wall-clock minutes on a 4 vCPU runner and 6,000 on a 1 vCPU one. A card is required before the first job, so this is not a no-card lane.
- evidence note: The included pool, the run-minute definition, the weighting and the card requirement are read from the vendor own pages. Raise by running one job on the included pool and reading the run-minute counter and the first invoice line.

## Semaphore Cloud

- `ci-cd-runners/semaphore-cloud` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding request-rate | category CI runner | tier free monthly credit
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-04T06:00:39.388Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-05
- url https://semaphore.io/pricing | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/semaphore.md
- free tier: USD 15 of free credits per month for every organization, about 2,000 Ubuntu x64 2-vCPU minutes; 20 concurrent jobs by default; no card | unit: credits | metered on: wall-clock | read on: 2026-10-30 | source: [1] | note: the credit is US dollars spent per minute at each machine's rate: f1-standard-2 (x64) USD 0.0075, r1-standard-2 (ARM) USD 0.003, a2-standard-4 (macOS) USD 0.09; a job under one minute is billed as one minute
- per-object cap: execution_time_limit is 1 hour by default and at most 24 hours (1,440 minutes); jobs are terminated at the limit, and a block or job limit longer than its pipeline's is rejected | source: [2] | note: no per-artifact size cap was found in the pages read
- retention: artifacts in the workflow and job namespaces are kept at most 400 days; project artifacts have no age limit; the agent and every file on it are discarded when the job ends | days: 400 | source: [3]
- egress: artifact egress is free up to 20 GB a month with 100 GB a month of artifact storage; beyond it USD 0.35 per GB of egress and USD 0.07 per GB of storage | metered: yes | free allowance: 20 GB of artifact egress a month | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: Sign-up needs a GitHub or Bitbucket account; the free usage is advertised as 'Start free — $15/mo, no card'; the flow then asks for an organization name and a short survey.
- interface: git, cli
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): USD 15 of credit a month: about 2,000 minutes on f1-standard-2 (2 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 45 GB disk) at USD 0.0075 a minute; USD 15 / USD 0.003 = 5,000 minutes on r1-standard-2 (ARM, 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM) [1]
  - request-rate (binding): 20 concurrent jobs by default; higher limits on request [1]
  - per-object-cap: 1 hour per pipeline by default, at most 24 hours (1,440 minutes) [2]
  - volume-quota: 20 GB a month of artifact egress and 100 GB a month of artifact storage free; then USD 0.35 per GB egress and USD 0.07 per GB storage [1]
  - retention-clamped: workflow and job artifacts are deleted after at most 400 days [3]
- limits note: 9.6 GB of cache storage per project; time spent queued for a concurrency slot is not billed; the FAQ states that open-source and free plans cannot create private projects
- binding note: the USD 15 credit is spent at about 2,000 f1-standard-2 minutes a month, long before 20 concurrent jobs or the 24-hour job ceiling bind; a monthly minute pool has no kind of its own and sits under request-rate as in the other hosted CI records
- interface detail: a pipeline YAML such as .semaphore/semaphore.yml in a GitHub or Bitbucket repository, or the visual workflow editor; the sem CLI opens an SSH session into a running job
- tooling: Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 images on F1 x86_64 machines with Docker environments, Ubuntu 24.04 on R1 ARM machines, macOS Xcode images on A2 machines; the toolbox commands checkout, cache, artifact, sem-version and sem-service; the sem-ai CLI and an MCP server. The Community Edition is Apache-2.0 software the user installs and runs on a rented or free machine, after every hosted offer
- composes with: a monthly dollar credit rather than a minute count, so the R1 ARM machine at USD 0.003 a minute stretches it furthest; artifacts leave free up to 20 GB a month, and the project artifact namespace has no age limit
- reliability: a job runs on an ephemeral agent destroyed at the end of the job; a shared runner address can already be at the Docker Hub anonymous pull limit
- notes: The pricing page names one free allowance, USD 15 a month for every organization. The Cloud page FAQ says Linux and macOS open-source projects get free parallel CI and gives no number, so any open-source allowance beyond the USD 15 is unverified. The Community Edition (Apache-2.0) is software the user installs and runs, the last resort after every hosted offer.
- evidence note: pricing, billing, machine-type, pipeline-YAML, artifact, FAQ and sign-up pages were read and quoted on 2026-10-30; no job was run. Raised to measured by a probe of a job on f1-standard-2.

## Vercel CI

- `ci-cd-runners/vercel-ci` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding volume-quota | category CI runner | tier Hobby
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-04T06:00:42.536Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-05
- url https://vercel.com/docs/ci | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/vercel.md
- free tier: Hobby: 200 CPU minutes a month included; a CPU minute is one CPU running for one minute. Pro: USD 0.0035 per CPU minute. Beta on all plans | unit: minutes | metered on: wall-clock | read on: 2026-11-02 | source: [1] | note: the true unit is CPU minutes (CPUs multiplied by task run time, rounded up to the second, 1 second minimum); the vocabulary has no core-minutes term, so unit is minutes. Each run spends 4 CPUs on bootstrapping and 2 CPUs by default on each task that runs; cached and skipped tasks cost nothing
- per-object cap: 2 CPUs and 4 GB of memory per task by default, up to 32 CPUs and 64 GB of memory with a ci:cpus tag; bootstrapping install step 4 CPUs and 8 GB by default. Job time limit: unverified: no Vercel CI page states a task or run time limit | source: [2]
- retention: unverified: no Vercel CI page states how long runs and task logs are kept | source: [3]
- egress: unverified: no Vercel CI page states a network egress policy for tasks; the network traffic of tasks passes through a Vercel CI certificate authority | metered: no | source: [4]
- identity: email | detail: a Vercel account opened with an email address (six-digit one-time password) or a Git provider; a GitHub repository connected to a Vercel project. No card is asked on Hobby; Pro adds USD 20 a month
- interface: git, cli, rest
- limits:
  - volume-quota (binding): 200 CPU minutes a month on Hobby; Pro USD 0.0035 per CPU minute [1]
  - per-object-cap: 2 CPUs and 4 GB of memory per task by default, up to 32 CPUs and 64 GB; install step 4 CPUs and 8 GB [2]
  - write-gated: GitHub repositories only, private repositories only, a git push as the only trigger, Linux only, Turborepo required [3]
- limits note: the job time limit and the largest task size available on Hobby are not stated on any page read; the 45-minute build limit of the Vercel limits page applies to deployment builds, not to Vercel CI tasks
- binding note: 200 CPU minutes a month are spent faster than wall-clock minutes because bootstrapping bills 4 CPUs by default and every task that runs bills 2 CPUs by default, so the monthly quota runs out before any size limit
- interface detail: a git push to a GitHub repository connected to a Vercel project runs every task tagged ci in turbo.json; a repository is enabled with the vercel ci enable command, runs and task logs are read in the dashboard CI tab, with the vercel ci CLI, the Vercel MCP and the REST API, and the status of the tasks is posted to the pull request as a check
- tooling: Turborepo 2.11.7 or later and Vercel CLI 64.3.1 or later; tasks run in Linux containers on x86_64, Amazon Linux 2023 by default or Ubuntu 24.04 with a ci:os:ubuntu tag, with Node.js 24, git, Docker and common build tools preinstalled; extra tools are installed during bootstrapping with an install command in vercel.json
- composes with: a hosted runner for tagged Turborepo tasks (lint, type check, tests, builds) triggered only by a git push to a private GitHub repository; it has no schedule, manual or pull-request trigger and no public-repository support, so GitHub Actions on a public repository and the other hosted runners of this topic come first for general jobs
- reliability: Beta: features and configuration may change; behaviour once the 200 Hobby CPU minutes are spent is unverified
- notes: Confirmed as a hosted CI runner: it runs the Turborepo tasks tagged ci (lint, type checks, tests, builds) on every git push, each task in its own isolated container. It is not a general workflow runner: no YAML workflows, no scheduled or manual triggers, GitHub private repositories only. Launched in Beta on 2026-10-28 on all plans. Whether Hobby can use the 32-CPU task size and what a run does after the Hobby allowance is spent are unverified.
- evidence note: every number is quoted from Vercel's pricing page and Vercel CI documentation; no run was made, so the job time limit, the largest task size on Hobby and the behaviour once the 200 CPU minutes are spent are unverified

## NixCI

- `ci-cd-runners/nixci` | trial-only | evidence documented | binding volume-quota | category CI runner | tier FOSS
- needs card unknown, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-09T12:54:40.941Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-10
- url https://nix-ci.com/pricing | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/nix-ci.md
- free tier: no free hosted compute beyond a trial: the FOSS plan is free with your own workers, hosted workers are billed at USD 0.33 an hour even on it, and new users get a 14-day trial on the demo system, after which builds stop. The demo needs no signup and builds the newest 3 commits of a repository | unit: none | metered on: none | read on: 2026-11-02 | source: [1] | note: the hosted plan is USD 37 a month per developer plus USD 0.33 per worker-hour; a developer is a person who pushes at least 3 commits to private repositories in a month
- per-object cap: unverified: the hosted worker and pricing pages state no per-job time limit | source: [2]
- retention: build logs are kept 60 days; build metadata 90 days; cached artefacts 90 days | days: 60 | source: [3]
- egress: not stated | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: sign-in is through a GitHub, GitLab or Codeberg account, held by installing the NixCI GitHub App on the repositories or by the equivalent GitLab or Codeberg webhook; the demo states that no signup or payment details are required. Beyond the trial the account takes a Subscribe step, which is behind a login wall, so unverified: behind a sign-up whether that step asks for a card. No phone number appears anywhere in the sign-up path
- interface: git
- limits:
  - volume-quota (binding): 14-day trial on the demo system; builds stop after it ends unless the account is upgraded [1]
  - volume-quota (binding): hosted workers billed at USD 0.3342 an hour per second of job execution, on every plan [2]
  - retention-clamped: build logs 60 days; build metadata and cached artefacts 90 days [3]
- limits note: the demo runs only the newest 3 commits of a repository
- binding note: hosted compute is paid by the second on every plan and the only free hosted use is the 14-day trial, so no free hosted allowance remains after it
- interface detail: a GitHub App, a GitLab or a Codeberg webhook runs CI for every repository that has a flake.nix, with no in-repo configuration required; results come back as commit statuses
- tooling: a flake.nix in the repository; the NixCI GitHub App, or a GitLab or Codeberg integration; hosted workers are 16 vCPU, 64 GiB RAM, 1 TB disk, x86_64-linux machines at Hetzner
- composes with: the hosted workers run x86_64-linux Nix builds, tests and deployments from a flake; a GitHub Actions job on a public repository comes first, and the user's own workers come last
- reliability: unverified: the vendor publishes no uptime figure or status page that was read
- notes: A hosted Nix CI exists with no free hosted allowance: the FOSS plan is free only when the user supplies the workers, and hosted worker time is paid by the second, so the offer is trial-only. Hosted runners of this topic come first. Last resort: the user's own workers, which NixCI offers to any subscriber on request. Sign-up is a GitHub, GitLab or Codeberg account through the forge App, and beyond the trial a Subscribe step follows; unverified: behind a sign-up whether that step asks for a card, so the card flag is left unknown rather than set to no.
- evidence note: every value is quoted from the vendor's pricing, workers, demo, getting-started and privacy pages; no sign-up was made, so the terms of the FOSS plan, the card requirement and any per-job time cap are unverified

## Actuated

- `ci-cd-runners/actuated` | paid-only | evidence documented | binding per-object-cap | category CI runner control plane | tier Self-Service
- needs card yes, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-06T16:14:44.903Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-07
- url https://actuated.com/pricing | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/actuated.md
- free tier: none at self-service: the Self-Service plan is a flat USD 150 a month for the first server and USD 125 for each additional, with unlimited build minutes and unlimited concurrency, and the servers are rented separately; the sponsored programme with the CNCF and Ampere grants no plan, no seat and no server, and the notes state what it does grant | unit: none | metered on: none | read on: 2026-11-04 | source: [1] | note: there is no list price per minute: the pricing table shows USD 0.005 per minute for every runner size against USD 0.008 for GitHub's 2-core hosted runner, which is the flat USD 150 spread over the workload the page's calculator assumes
- per-object cap: not stated as a number: a job is bounded by one server's vCPU and RAM, chosen per job with a runs-on label such as actuated-2cpu-8gb | source: [2]
- retention: each job runs in a microVM created for it and removed immediately after; server metrics are kept 14 days | source: [3]
- egress: not stated by Actuated: jobs run on the rented server, so traffic leaves under that server provider's terms | metered: no | source: [4]
- identity: card | detail: a GitHub organisation with admin access to install the actuated GitHub App, and a company credit card for the monthly subscription; the agent's Account API Token is issued on request; the sponsored CNCF programme is requested through the vendor's form instead of a subscription
- interface: git
- limits:
  - per-object-cap (binding): a job is bounded by one server's vCPU and RAM; the plan sets how many servers may run [4]
  - retention-clamped: an autoenrolled agent offline for 15 minutes is removed automatically; jobs queue until a server is ready [5]
- limits note: no minute cap: unlimited build minutes, RAM, CPUs and concurrency at a flat rate per server; plans are paid monthly with no minimum commitment; Linux only, AMD64 or 64-bit Arm; a GitHub organisation, not a personal account, and an organisation admin to install the GitHub App
- binding note: no free allowance, so the card and the plan price fail first; inside a plan the minutes are unlimited and the size of one rented server bounds every job
- interface detail: a GitHub Actions workflow targets the fleet with runs-on: actuated or a sized label such as actuated-2cpu-8gb; GitLab CI is also supported. The control plane schedules each job into a Firecracker microVM on a Linux server, x86_64 or 64-bit Arm, that runs the Actuated agent
- endpoint: https://github.com/apps/self-actuated
- tooling: the user rents a Linux server with KVM, bare metal or a cloud VM with nested virtualisation, and runs the Actuated agent on it; Actuated runs the control plane, the GitHub App and the managed VM images, and issues the Account API Token the agent installer needs
- composes with: the monthly floor is the USD 150 plan plus a rented server, which the vendor prices at 40-50 EUR a month at the low end of bare metal; GitHub Actions on a public repository stays free and comes first
- reliability: the control plane holds jobs in a queue while no enrolled server is online, and drops an autoenrolled agent that has been offline for 15 minutes
- notes: Paid only at self-service, and the one documented zero-cost route is the sponsored programme with the CNCF and Ampere. That programme is neither a plan, a seat nor a server of the project's own: it grants a selected project a share of a sponsor-funded pool of Arm64 runners that the vendor operates, shared with every other participating project, and reached with the same runs-on label as a paid fleet. The published pool is 20 build slots shared between all CNCF projects. It is limited to CNCF projects and to Arm CI only, so a project outside the CNCF cannot join it; the vendor granted access to individual non-CNCF projects case by case, runc among them, which it calls an OCI project under the Linux Foundation rather than a CNCF project while counting its minutes in the programme's totals, and it separately lists Atuin, runc and criu among the open-source projects it has sponsored, without naming the programme. A sponsored project keeps its own GitHub organisation, where a maintainer installs the Actuated GitHub App, and it must add the Actuated badge to the top of the README of every repository that uses the runners. The first one-year pilot filled every slot by March 2024, after which the vendor offered a discounted subscription to a company that would fund a maintainer's time. The vendor's FAQ still listed the programme when it was read on 2026-11-04, but no page states whether it accepts projects now, and the Arm servers it ran on were hosted by Equinix Metal, which ended service on 2026-06-30, so its current status is unverified. Hosted runners with a free allowance in this topic come first.
- evidence note: the price, the plan terms and the registration requirements are quoted from the vendor's pricing page and documentation; no account was opened
- self hosted: no

## Cloudflare Artifacts

- `ci-cd-runners/cloudflare-artifacts` | paid-only | evidence documented | binding write-gated | category CI runner control plane | tier Workers Paid
- needs card yes, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-02T15:23:42.470Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-03
- url https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/cloudflare.md
- free tier: none on Workers Free: Artifacts is unavailable there. Workers Paid (USD 5 a month minimum) includes the first 10,000 operations and the first 1 GB of storage each month, then USD 0.15 per additional 1,000 operations and USD 0.50 per additional GB-month; billing for both starts on 2026-11-12 | unit: none | metered on: none | read on: 2026-11-02 | source: [1] | note: the Paid allowance is 10,000 operations and 1 GB-month of storage a month, inside a plan that costs USD 5 a month; the pricing table names no Workers Free allowance
- per-object cap: 32 MiB per file, 64 MiB per push, 50,000 objects per push | source: [2]
- retention: repositories remain stored until they are explicitly deleted | source: [1]
- egress: unverified: the Artifacts pricing page lists two billed dimensions, operations and storage, and states nothing about egress | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: card | detail: sign-up needs an email address and a password; Workers Paid needs a primary payment method (card, PayPal or a wallet) on the billing profile
- interface: git, rest
- limits:
  - write-gated (binding): not available on Workers Free; Workers Paid (USD 5 a month minimum) is required [3]
  - volume-quota: 1 GB per repository for repos created on or after 2026-09-29, 10 GB for earlier repos; 1 TB per account, raisable on request; repositories and namespaces unlimited [2]
  - per-object-cap: 32 MiB per file; 64 MiB and 50,000 objects per push [2]
  - request-rate: 2,000 Git requests per 10 seconds per artifact; 2,000 control-plane requests per 10 seconds per namespace [2]
- limits note: the account ceiling of 1 TB and the per-repository ceiling apply on top of the billed 1 GB included; the per-repository ceiling was 10 GB before 2026-09-29
- binding note: the service is not available on the Workers Free plan; a Workers Paid subscription, which needs a payment method, is required before any repository can be created
- interface detail: a Workers binding, a REST API and the Git smart-HTTP protocol over one repository; any standard Git client clones and pushes to the repository's remote URL with a short-lived repository token; Workers Builds can build and deploy a Worker from a repository
- endpoint: https://artifacts.cloudflare.net/v1/api/namespaces/<NAMESPACE>/repos
- tooling: a standard Git client, the Cloudflare REST API with an API token, or the Artifacts binding in a Worker; ArtifactFS is also documented for filesystem access
- composes with: source hosting for Workers Builds on the same account: a push to the production branch builds and deploys the Worker, other branches create Worker Previews. No runner of its own: it stores code and does not execute jobs. GitHub or GitLab hosting comes first for a free account
- reliability: Artifacts is in open beta (announced 2026-10-01); billing was first announced for 2026-10-14 and the pricing page now says 2026-11-12
- notes: Not usable on Workers Free: the docs state usage is unavailable there, so the free-account answer is no. On Workers Paid it is Git-compatible storage with 1 GB of storage and 10,000 operations included each month; its CI relevance is as a source repository for Workers Builds. Per-repository storage was 10 GB for repos created before 2026-09-29 and is 1 GB after.
- evidence note: every value is quoted from Cloudflare's Artifacts documentation pages read on 2026-11-02; no repository was created, the dashboard sign-up and plan upgrade were not passed, and egress terms for Artifacts are unverified

## Codefresh CI (Octopus Deploy)

- `ci-cd-runners/codefresh-ci` | paid-only | evidence documented | binding write-gated | category CI runner
- needs card no, phone yes, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-04T06:00:39.389Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-05
- url https://codefresh.io/docs/docs/pipelines/run-pipeline/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/codefresh.md
- free tier: no free hosted runner: a free account runs pipelines only on a Hybrid Runner in a Kubernetes cluster the user provides; Cloud Builds (the SaaS runtime) are disabled for all accounts by default and enabled on an admin request answered within 24 hours; codefresh.io/pricing/ now serves Octopus Deploy pricing, which lists no Codefresh plan | unit: none | metered on: none | read on: 2026-10-30 | source: [1] | note: the pricing page as archived on 2024-01-04 offered a free Community plan: up to 5 developers, 1000 cloud credits a month, unlimited hybrid builds and 1 week of data retention; at 5 credits a minute on the S machine that is 1000 / 5 = 200 minutes
- per-object cap: unverified: no build duration limit for the SaaS runtime was found in the pages read | source: [1]
- retention: build and log data are kept for six months, for SaaS and on-premises installations | source: [1]
- egress: unverified: no egress terms for the SaaS runtime were found in the pages read | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: any-phone | detail: sign-up through GitHub, Bitbucket, GitLab, Azure, Google or LDAP, then a phone number with a country code verified by a sent code, then organization details and use cases
- interface: git, cli
- limits:
  - write-gated (binding): Cloud Builds are disabled for all accounts by default; an account admin requests them and the answer takes up to 24 hours [1]
  - retention-clamped: build and log data are kept six months [1]
- limits note: SaaS memory limits are Small 1 GB, Medium 4 GB and Large 8 GB; pipeline concurrency is a per-pipeline setting from 0 to 14 or unlimited, and no plan concurrency limit was found; by default a build step that prints nothing to the log for 45 minutes is terminated; no build duration limit and no monthly cloud credit allowance for a Cloud Builds grant were found in the pages read
- binding note: no hosted build runs until Codefresh grants Cloud Builds to the account; without the grant the only runtime is a Hybrid Runner on infrastructure the user supplies
- interface detail: a Codefresh pipeline triggered from a Git provider integration; the codefresh CLI
- tooling: SaaS machine sizes from S (1 CPU, 1 GB) to XXL (16 CPU, 32 GB), billed in cloud credits, once Cloud Builds are granted. The free path is the Hybrid Runner, which the user installs and runs in a Kubernetes cluster on rented or free machines; it comes after any hosted runtime
- composes with: no hosted capacity without a Cloud Builds grant; the hosted control plane can drive a Hybrid Runner placed on a free compute offer
- reliability: Octopus Deploy acquired Codefresh in February 2024; Codefresh CI remains available for customers, and the Codefresh pricing URL redirects to Octopus Deploy pricing
- notes: No free hosted runner today: a new free account gets the hosted control plane and must bring a Kubernetes cluster for the Hybrid Runner, while Cloud Builds are granted on request with no published allowance or price. The 1000-credit Community plan of January 2024 is gone from the live pricing URL.
- evidence note: the Codefresh documentation, the Octopus Deploy Codefresh pages and the live and archived pricing pages were read and quoted on 2026-10-30; the sign-up app is a login wall and was not passed, so the outcome of a Cloud Builds request is unverified.

## SourceHut builds.sr.ht

- `ci-cd-runners/sourcehut-builds` | paid-only | evidence documented | binding write-gated | category CI runner | tier paid account
- needs card yes, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-04T06:00:39.390Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-05
- url https://man.sr.ht/builds.sr.ht/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/sr.md
- free tier: no free allowance: builds.sr.ht requires a paid account (EUR 4 or USD 4 a month at the lowest tier, every tier with the same service and limits) for users registered on or after 2021-05-01; free service is issued to a user who emails support explaining that they cannot pay | unit: none | metered on: none | read on: 2026-10-30 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: 1 GiB per artifact file; the hosted build time limit is not published, the documented SSH message reads 'Your VM will be terminated 4 hours from now', and the software's example configuration sets a 45-minute maximum build duration | bytes: 1073741824 | source: [2]
- retention: artifacts are uploaded only for successful jobs and pruned after 90 days | days: 90 | source: [2]
- egress: unverified: no egress terms were found in the pages read | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: card | detail: a meta.sr.ht account registered as a maintainer with payment by credit card, SEPA direct debit, iDEAL or Bancontact; free service is issued on an emailed request to support; a contributor account without payment cannot submit builds
- interface: git, ssh, graphql, cli
- limits:
  - write-gated (binding): submitting build jobs needs a paid account; free service only after an emailed request to support [3]
  - per-object-cap: 1 GiB per artifact file [2]
  - retention-clamped: artifacts pruned after 90 days, uploaded only for successful jobs [2]
- limits note: the hosted runner size and per-user concurrency are not published; the build image control script boots each VM with 2 CPUs and 4096 MB of memory unless configured otherwise, and a build host of 16 cores and 128 GB supports up to 16 parallel build slots; a failed build's VM stays up 10 more minutes for SSH
- binding note: nothing runs without a payment or an aid grant; once paid, every tier has the same service limits
- interface detail: a YAML build manifest submitted through the API, the web form at builds.sr.ht/submit, a manifest in a git.sr.ht or hg.sr.ht repository, patches sent to a mailing list, or the hut CLI; SSH into a running or failed build VM
- tooling: full virtual machines with root through sudo, on x86_64 images (the only native architecture in the image table); the hut CLI. SourceHut is AGPL-3.0 software the user can install and run on a rented or free machine, which comes after the hosted service
- composes with: a paid or aid-granted account gets full VMs with root and SSH access; artifacts leave through the jobs page and are pruned at 90 days
- reliability: the service is in public alpha; from the beta, unpaid accounts become read-only for their own projects, with at least 60 days notice by email; pricing is set to change after the alpha
- notes: Not free hosted CI: builds.sr.ht has needed a paid account since 2021-05-01, at EUR 4 or USD 4 a month for the whole service, with free service granted on an emailed request. The hosted runner size, job time limit and concurrency are not published; the repository defaults are 2 CPUs, 4096 MB and 45 minutes.
- evidence note: the pricing, billing FAQ, builds billing-change, alpha, builds and manifest pages were read and quoted on 2026-10-30; runner size and the 45-minute timeout come from the open-source repository's defaults, not from the hosted service, and no build was run.

## Harness CI Free plan (Harness Cloud)

- `ci-cd-runners/harness-ci-free` | fails-identity | evidence documented | binding request-rate | category CI runner | tier Free
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution yes | verified 2026-11-04T06:00:39.389Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-05
- url https://developer.harness.io/continuous-integration/troubleshooting-and-resources/ci-subscription-mgmt | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/harness.md
- free tier: Free plans receive 2,000 Harness Cloud credits every month, and unused credits expire at month end; Linux xsmall (2 cores, 7 GB) costs 1 credit a minute and Linux small (4 cores, 15 GB) 2 credits a minute | unit: credits | metered on: wall-clock | read on: 2026-10-30 | source: [1] | note: the pricing page's Free plan lists Harness Open Source, Litmus Chaos and community support and names no CI module or Harness Cloud allowance; the Harness Cloud product page and the CI documentation state the 2,000 a month
- per-object cap: on the Free plan a stage times out at 1 hour and a pipeline at 2 hours; each CI stage runs in a new ephemeral VM | source: [2]
- retention: unverified: no log or artifact retention period for the Free plan was found in the pages read; cache above the 2 GB Free limit evicts the oldest caches | source: [1]
- egress: network transfer from Harness Cloud to customer-managed storage is limited to 1 GB on Free, 5 GB on Startup and 10 GB on Enterprise | metered: yes | free allowance: 1 GB of network transfer to customer-managed storage | source: [1]
- identity: institution | detail: Harness Cloud on the Free plan is limited to business email domains, with Gmail, Hotmail, Yahoo and other unverified domains blocked, and Free plans require credit card validation to use it; the Harness Cloud product page says 'No credit card required', which the CI documentation contradicts
- interface: git
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): 2,000 credits a month on Free, unused credits expire; Linux xsmall (2 cores, 7 GB) 1 credit a minute, Linux small (4 cores, 15 GB) 2 credits a minute [1]
  - request-rate (binding): 2 concurrent pipeline executions per account on the Free plan, not editable; 2 concurrent steps or stages within one execution [2]
  - request-rate (binding): Harness Cloud concurrent stages on Free: Linux 20, Windows 1, macOS 1 [1]
  - per-object-cap: stage timeout 1 hour and pipeline timeout 2 hours on the Free plan [2]
  - volume-quota: 1 GB of network transfer from Harness Cloud to customer-managed storage on Free [1]
- limits note: 2 GB of CI Intelligence cache storage on Free, with the oldest caches evicted beyond it; use beyond the credits continues and is invoiced in arrears
- binding note: identity binds before any limit: Harness Cloud on Free needs card validation and a business email domain. Among the limits, the 2,000 monthly credits are 2,000 xsmall minutes, about 33 hours (2,000 / 60); the 1-hour stage timeout binds first for any single long job
- interface detail: a Harness pipeline built in the visual editor or YAML, with a CI stage on Harness Cloud infrastructure and a Git connector to the repository
- tooling: Harness-managed VMs: Linux AMD64 and ARM64 from 2 to 96 cores, Windows, and macOS on Apple M4; Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 images with preinstalled tools; steps run on the VM or in a Docker container. The local runner, which the user installs and runs on a machine of their own, rented or free, has no build limit and needs no card; it comes after the hosted offer
- composes with: 2,000 Linux xsmall minutes a month behind a card check and a business email domain; the 1 GB transfer limit to outside storage makes it a place to run work rather than to ship large outputs
- reliability: credits used beyond the allowance are invoiced in arrears, and Harness may suspend Harness Cloud executions when they are not paid
- notes: The allowance is real on paper, 2,000 credits a month with 20 concurrent Linux stages, but the account-wide limit of 2 concurrent pipeline executions and the 1-hour stage timeout make it small, and the gate in front of it is a business email domain plus card validation. The Developer 360 post (updated 2026-09-30) lists Continuous Integration among the Free plan modules and the CI documentation still states the 2,000 credits, although the pricing page's Free plan names no CI module; whether a new Free account receives the credits, and whether a custom-domain address passes the business-domain check, is unverified: behind a sign-up.
- evidence note: the CI subscription, Harness Cloud and pipeline settings documentation, the pricing page and the Harness Cloud product page were read and quoted on 2026-10-30; the sign-up gate itself is a single-page app and was not passed. Raised by a sign-up outcome with a generic and a custom-domain address.

## Forgejo and Gitea Actions (self-hosted)

- `ci-cd-runners/forgejo-gitea-actions` | self-hosted, last resort | verdict qualifies | evidence documented | binding none | category CI software
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-06T19:14:28.503Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-07
- url https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/user/actions/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/forgejo.md
- free tier: GPL v3+ for Forgejo v9.0 and later, MIT for Forgejo up to v8.0 | unit: unlimited | metered on: none | read on: 2026-11-06 | source: [1] | note: Gitea, the upstream project, is licensed under the MIT License.
- per-object cap: a job runs for at most the number of minutes its jobs.<job_id>.timeout-minutes key sets | source: [2] | note: the actual machine provided by the runner entirely depends on how the runner was registered
- retention: whatever the runner host retains | source: [2]
- egress: whatever the runner host charges | metered: no | source: [2]
- identity: anonymous | detail: the software needs no account
- interface: git, cli
- limits:
  - per-object-cap: a job runs for at most the number of minutes its jobs.<job_id>.timeout-minutes key sets [2]
- interface detail: a .forgejo/workflows or .gitea/workflows YAML; the act runner; a compatible subset of GitHub Actions
- tooling: the forgejo or act runner binary; docker or a host backend
- composes with: Actions syntax without GitHub, which lets a workflow move between a free hosted runner and your own machine without a rewrite
- reliability: compatibility with GitHub Actions is a documented subset, so a workflow that runs on GitHub may need edits
- notes: The compatibility is the value and the subset is the cost. A workflow that depends on a GitHub-only action does not run.
- evidence note: the Forgejo Actions user guide was read; Codeberg's hosted instance runs the same software.
- self hosted: yes
- evidence:
  - [2] 2026-10-22: Forgejo Actions is GitHub-Actions-compatible with documented differences; runners are user-provided
  - [3] 2026-10-22: Codeberg's hosted runners use ghcr.io/catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest to provide a compatibility level with GitHub Actions, and Docker-in-Docker is not officially supported
  - [2] 2026-11-04: Forgejo Actions is not identical to GitHub Actions, so a workflow may need edits | capture: sha256:8c8a779c1a4e82b1679b0238872cb7c0a41dee2aa0046ff47932817138faf289 | quote: However, GitHub Actions and Forgejo Actions are not the same and things might not work right away.
  - [1] 2026-11-06: Forgejo v9.0 and later is GPL v3+ and Forgejo up to v8.0 is MIT | capture: sha256:09c8f6b9e7c660821c31c34a03ecd1c32b6731755ab183f685b753b9af7b5a8f | quote: Forgejo versions v9.0 and later are distributed under the terms of the GPL v3+. ... Forgejo versions up to v8.0 inclusive are distributed under the terms of the MIT license.
  - [4] 2026-11-06: Gitea is licensed under the MIT License | capture: sha256:f44bcff37456431faa23c5d19b75db142fc191e3e0ef0d70c60bd4ceee5aea3a | quote: This project is licensed under the MIT License.
  - [2] 2026-11-06: the jobs.<job_id>.timeout-minutes key caps how long a job runs | capture: sha256:8c8a779c1a4e82b1679b0238872cb7c0a41dee2aa0046ff47932817138faf289 | quote: Set the number of minutes this job can be performed before it is canceled.
  - [2] 2026-11-06: the machine a job gets depends on how the runner was registered | capture: sha256:8c8a779c1a4e82b1679b0238872cb7c0a41dee2aa0046ff47932817138faf289 | quote: The actual machine provided by the runner entirely depends on how the runner was registered
